My photosynthesis chapters

Year 4 Science · LS 4.2.1, 4.2.2 and 4.2.3 · Read, play and tell a partner.

1. Meaning

Photosynthesis is a process where plants make their own food.

Word-piece game: Put these pieces in order, then say the whole meaning: their own food / a process / make / where plants.

2. Needs

  • Sunlight: energy from the Sun.
  • Water: absorbed through roots.
  • Carbon dioxide: a gas in the air that enters leaves.
  • Chlorophyll: the green substance in plants that absorbs sunlight.

Collect & Avoid on paper: Write the four needs on small pieces of paper. Add three distractions: a toy, a sweet and a storybook. Mix them. Collect only the needs. If you choose a distraction, name a need to try again.

Chlorophyll is already inside plants. Collecting its word card is just a game.

My challenge: Name at least two needs without looking.

3. Products

Plants make glucose, a sugar used as food. Some glucose is stored as starch. Oxygen is released through leaves. The two products to remember are starch and oxygen.

Observe the products picture on page 78 of Science Year 4, or revisit the website’s two animated models. Tell a partner what you notice about stored food and released gas.

Product post office: Make two signs: NEED and PRODUCT. Deliver cards for starch, water, oxygen and sunlight to the right sign.

My challenge: Identify and name at least one product.

My discoveries

Explain the meaning of photosynthesis. Name two needs. Name one product.

Nico’s forest is an optional online game for fun after the chapters.

Partner’s answer guide

Meaning: a process where plants make their own food. Needs: sunlight, water, carbon dioxide, chlorophyll. Products: starch, oxygen.

Source: Science Year 4 · printed pages 76–78. These activities practise three learning objectives; they do not assign official performance levels.
